title: Stripe-aware pipeline convergence for prefill/decode overlap
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a stripe-aware pipeline convergence layer that coordinates token microstripe assignment across tensor/pipeline parallel stages to maximize NCCL overlap during prefill and decode phases while preserving low tail latency for single-token hot paths.
background: We regularly see suboptimal NCCL utilization during mixed prefill+decode workloads on heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters. Current token routing uses coarse-grained microbatches which creates synchronization points that prevent overlap between all-reduce/transpose communication and kernel execution. Earlier tickets focused on staged rendezvous and microbatch routing, but customer workloads with a mix of many short decodes and occasional long prefill sequences still hit 99th percentile latency spikes. This ticket experiments with a stripe-aware convergence mechanism that slices token waves into aligned stripes across pipeline ranks, provides kernel selection hints to the local runtime, and schedules opportunistic NCCL windows to hide comm latency behind decode kernels.
objectives: 1) Reduce 95th/99th percentile single-request latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads by at least 20% on our internal benchmark. 2) Improve NCCL link utilization on heterogeneous clusters (A100+H100 mixes) by >15% for sustained prefill-heavy bursts. 3) Integrate with kernel-selection hints so attention kernels and fused-norm ops are scheduled to maximize comm compute overlap without violating latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Bench pipeline shows >=20% reduction in 95th latency for mixed workload (internal perf harness).
NCCL link utilization dashboard (per-job view) shows >=15% uplift vs baseline for target bursts.
Automated regression tests added for stripe boundary correctness and deterministic ordering under reordering faults.
PR merged with runtime tests passing and no regressions in existing microbatching suites.
Feature flag guarded rollout and kill-switch implemented in control-plane config.
implementation_notes: Introduce StripeAllocator component in the conductor to compute per-token stripe assignments across pipeline ranks.
Expose kernel_hints API to the local executor (hint types: ATTENTION_FUSE, TRANSPOSE_EARLY, KV_PREFETCH) with low-cost best-effort semantics.
Add NCCLWindow object that can be requested by runtime phases; windows have priority and optional preemption for latency-critical token streams.
Maintain determinism by attaching stripe metadata to request trace so replay/recording tools can reproduce ordering.
Fallback path: if heterogeneity or slot constraints prevent stripe alignment, gracefully degrade to current microbatch router with telemetry tag.
performance_targets: 95th latency: -20% vs baseline on mixed 70% decode / 30% prefill synthetic workload
Throughput: no more than 5% regression on throughput-heavy pure-prefill workloads
NCCL average link utilization: +15% for target burst patterns
Memory overhead: stripe metadata <= 0.5% additional per-request memory
testing_plan: Unit tests for StripeAllocator assignments including edge cases (uneven GPU counts, disabled ranks).
Integration tests: multi-node perf harness with pinned model and mixed workload scenarios (short decodes interleaved with long prefill).
Chaos tests: inject delayed grpc/heartbeat between ranks to validate fallback and no-deadlock behavior.
Repro harness: record/replay capability to reproduce tail latency incidents in CI.
Benchmark runs: run against runtime-1.20 baseline and collect p50/p95/p99 and NCCL counters.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime config: runtime.features.stripe_convergence = false by default.
Canary: enable on 3 dedicated clusters that represent high-throughput, heterogeneous hardware.
Monitor for error rates, latency regressions, and NCCL errors for 72 hours before expanding rollout.
If regressions observed, use control-plane kill-switch and merge hotfix to revert stripe alignment in conductor.
monitoring_and_metrics: Per-request stripe_assignment metric with histogram of stripe sizes.
Kernel overlap efficiency: fraction of time comm overlaps decode kernel execution.
Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 per-route and per-model with stripe_convergence tag.
Incidents: track any NCCL errors with stripe_convergence=true as high priority.
open_questions: How aggressive should preemption of NCCL windows be for latency-critical single-token decodes?
Should kernel_hints be advisory only or can the scheduler enforce ordering that may penalize throughput?
Best telemetry dimensions to attribute improvements to stripe logic vs kernel selection changes?
Compatibility concerns when customers pin older model binaries that expect older microbatch boundaries.
